system_description.narrative_title: ECB leadership change amid Eurozone slowdown and French crisis
system_description.narrative_summary: A convergence of forces — an early Christine Lagarde exit from the ECB, weakening euro‑area growth and acute fiscal stress in France — is driving a dominant narrative of monetary-policy uncertainty feeding financial-market strain and political unrest. Key systemic variables are monetary-policy credibility, sovereign bond spreads, fiscal deficits, growth momentum and social stability; concrete entities include the ECB, national governments (notably France), rating agencies and banks. Feedback loops (higher yields → tighter financing → slower growth → political backlash) make this an open system with multiple amplifying and dampening interactions.
system_description.scope: The eurozone macro‑financial system over the coming quarters: ECB leadership and policy transmission; national fiscal positions (especially France); sovereign bond and banking sector dynamics; energy supply tensions that affect prices; and attendant political stability and public protest across EU members.
system_description.super_system: The global economy and international financial markets (including geopolitics, commodity markets and global investor sentiment).
adjacent_subsystems: National politics in EU member states (France, Italy, Germany)
European financial sector and capital markets (banks, sovereign bond markets, ratings)
Energy and commodity markets (gas storage, supply spikes)
EU institutions and fiscal governance (European Commission, Council, EU trade/policy rules)

variables.name: Monetary policy credibility
variables.description: Market and public belief in the predictability, competence and commitment of monetary policy makers to their stated objectives.

variables.name: Sovereign bond spreads
variables.description: The average premium investors demand over a benchmark for holding sovereign debt, reflecting perceived sovereign credit risk.

variables.name: Fiscal deficit level
variables.description: The size of the budget shortfall relative to the economy, measured as the gap between government expenditures and revenues.

variables.name: GDP growth momentum
variables.description: The recent rate of change in economic output indicating acceleration or deceleration of real GDP growth.

variables.name: Social stability
variables.description: The general level of societal order and calm, encompassing propensity for protests, strikes and civil unrest.

variables.name: Inflation rate
variables.description: The rate at which the general price level for goods and services is rising over a given period.

variables.name: Policy uncertainty
variables.description: The perceived unpredictability and ambiguity around future economic policy decisions and their timing.

variables.name: Banking sector solvency
variables.description: The aggregate capacity of banks to meet long‑term obligations and absorb losses without breaching capital thresholds.

variables.name: Banking sector liquidity
variables.description: The availability of short‑term funding and liquid assets across the banking system to meet payment and withdrawal needs.

variables.name: Energy price volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of short‑term swings in energy prices that affect production costs and inflation.

variables.name: Credit availability
variables.description: The ease and terms on which businesses and households can obtain loans and other forms of external finance.

variables.name: Investor risk appetite
variables.description: The collective willingness of financial investors to accept risk in pursuit of returns, influencing asset allocation and flows.

variables.name: Exchange rate volatility
variables.description: The degree of short‑term fluctuation in the currency exchange rate that affects trade competitiveness and capital flows.

variables.name: Political fragmentation
variables.description: The extent of division and dispersion of power across political actors and parties affecting government coherence and decision making.

variables.name: Public protest intensity
variables.description: The frequency, scale and violence level of collective public demonstrations and strikes unfolding over time.

variables.name: Fiscal adjustment rate
variables.description: The speed and scale at which fiscal policy (spending and taxation) is being tightened or loosened over time.

catalysts.title: Lagarde steps down (effective Feb 2027)
catalysts.description: Christine Lagarde's announced early resignation taking effect in February will create a formal leadership change at the ECB.
